clue.text: Blooming extravagance?

parts.note: read literally, the quality of being full of blooms; in fact a florid, over-ornate style of speech or writing

explanation.surface: A garden bursting with too many flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'Blooming' points to flowers, while the word means an over-decorated style.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid, ornate language is called flowery, and the noun names that over-elaborate quality.

clue.text: Cyril's odd ode

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange or out of order, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Cyril has written a peculiar poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a kind of song-like poem, the type of verse called a lyric.

clue.text: Employment of one skilled artificer

parts.note: employment means work
one, as in a person, is a man

explanation.surface: A craftsman finds a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a craftsman, and a skilled manual labourer is a workman.

clue.text: Reprimand engineers who are going round the islands

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps

indicators.note: going round tells us the verb's letters are wrapped around the islands

parts.note: are is a form of the verb to be
the UK, the United Kingdom, is a group of islands

explanation.surface: Engineers touring an archipelago get told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is only a link. 'the islands' stands for the United Kingdom, a nation made up of islands, and 'going round' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to scold or tell them off sharply.

clue.text: Uncharged particle in tune or discordant

indicators.note: discordant music is out of tune, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A musical paradox: a note either in tune or out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle carries no electric charge, which is where its name ('little neutral one') comes from.

clue.text: Stay second

definitions.meaning: a stay is a prop or brace holding something up
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop and to second is to back someone; both senses are about bearing or backing up.

clue.text: Highly regarded with spring in mind

parts.note: a spring of water is a well
something held in mind has been thought of

explanation.surface: Someone well respected, with spring on their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being esteemed or respected by others is the meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: Physicist of the naughty nineties

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so these letters misbehave and rearrange

explanation.surface: A scientist from the naughty nineties, the 1890s decade of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert of relativity fame is the best-known theoretical physicist.

clue.text: Where to find an exhibitor even now quite motionless

parts.note: an exhibitor at a trade show is found at a stand
even now means still

explanation.surface: Trade show visitors find the exhibitors frozen in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Not moving at all, like a vehicle stopped dead, is this idiom's meaning.

clue.text: One is not right to make one

definitions.text: One is not right to make one

parts.words: One is not right to make one
parts.note: anyone who is wrong has made a mistake: the clue reads as a moral riddle

explanation.surface: A riddle about wrongdoing and making something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'one' stands for the answer: a person who is wrong makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wrong and making a mistake are the same thing.

clue.text: Plan to show an indecent picture

parts.note: blue jokes or films are indecent
a print is a picture

explanation.surface: Someone means to display a dirty photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed design or scheme, like an architect's drawing, is this kind of plan.

clue.text: It is easy to find holes in her work

definitions.text: It is easy to find holes in her work

parts.words: It is easy to find holes in her work
parts.note: sounds like criticism of a sloppy worker, but describes a craftswoman whose fabric is full of deliberate holes

explanation.surface: A dig at someone whose work is full of flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find holes in' means 'criticise', but lace is a fabric made of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is an openwork fabric, so anyone producing it makes work full of gaps.

clue.text: Resting places needed with the sea so rough!

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors seek a refuge because the sea is so stormy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the desert, a fertile spot with water is where travellers stop to rest.

clue.text: Greedy person has to transgress in watering the plants

indicators.note: in says the sin goes inside the greedy person

parts.note: a hog is a greedy person
to transgress is to sin

explanation.surface: A glutton breaks the rules while tending the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Spraying a garden with a hose is how the plants get water.

clue.text: Take place of another endlessly flexible worker

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: supple means flexible
a worker is an ant, the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A bendy employee takes someone else's spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust and replace someone is to take their position.

clue.text: Curse two articles by the graduate

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A grammar pedant swears over articles beside a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' gives its own letters as a third article; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ban of excommunication is a church's solemn curse.

clue.text: Looks for and notices chief is inside

indicators.note: is inside tells us the chief word sits within the noticing word

parts.note: notices means sees
arch means chief, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: A police leader is in the building, looking for clues.
explanation.definitionFit: To search means to hunt or look for something.

clue.text: One in France put out of the first three

parts.note: un is French for one
put means placed

explanation.surface: A French entrant is moved aside and misses a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, a runner not finishing in the top places is said to be this.

clue.text: One goddess or another encompassing a heavenly body

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the goddess's name wraps the heavenly body

parts.note: another goddess: Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: Two goddesses vie over a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One goddess or another' reads as a choice between two deities. In fact the first is the definition and 'another' means a second goddess, the Greek spirit of ruin, whom 'encompassing' wraps round the heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenician fertility deity worshipped as queen of heaven is this goddess.

clue.text: Complained when I had shortly broken down

indicators.note: broken down means smashed up, so the letters reorganise

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: A motorist moaned after the car broke down.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan or grumble in a high voice is to complain.

clue.text: Assisting the man on record almost complete

parts.note: he means the man
an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: almost tells us to drop the last letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A man nearly finishes a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful that aids another is giving help.

clue.text: Maps spread out on an eastern boat

indicators.note: spread out suggests unfolding, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Charts are laid out on board an Oriental vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed skiff used in China and South East Asia is this vessel.

clue.text: Ambassador gives money back to the slave

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
L is pounds, from the Latin libra

indicators.note: back means the word to is reversed

explanation.surface: An ambassador hands cash back to a slave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link; 'back' reverses TO to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf in ancient Sparta was a helot, so the word means a slave.

clue.text: Nobleman correct going round to put it on the back of the vehicle

definitions.text: it on the back of the vehicle

indicators.note: going round tells us the word for correct encircles the nobleman

parts.note: correct means right
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat fixes something on the back of his car.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp fixed to the back of a car or bicycle is this light.

clue.text: General concession

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was a US Civil War general

explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses was a Union commander, and a sum awarded or allowed is a concession.

clue.text: How sniper could get possession

indicators.note: could suggests what the letters might turn into when rearranged

explanation.surface: A sniper wonders how to take something over.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something means having it in your possession.

clue.text: Trouble father first who is very weak

indicators.note: first says the father comes before the trouble

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
to trouble is to ail

explanation.surface: A father is ill and very weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Being feeble or delicate is to be very weak.

clue.text: Only a priest became a celebrity

indicators.note: became means turned into, so these letters change into something new

explanation.surface: A humble clergyman became a famous star.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous person, like a TV star, is called a personality.
